claims.text: The as-deposited material is a non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloy.
The as-deposited alloy has a predominantly ordered, single-phase hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited alloy exhibits a sharp, hysteretic magnetostructural transition.
A brief post-deposition anneal can induce nanoscale compositional ordering.
A brief post-deposition anneal can reduce grain-boundary heterogeneity.
A suitably tuned anneal can alleviate residual strain without significant grain coarsening.
Annealing will produce a more homogeneous microstructure through increased compositional ordering and reduced grain-boundary disorder.
Relieving internal strain and making grain-boundary ordering more uniform will decouple magnetic ordering from lattice distortions.
Lattice distortions associated with the magnetostructural transition drive hysteretic losses.
The proposed microstructural changes will broaden the magnetostructural transition and make it less abrupt.
The annealed samples will have a smaller hysteresis-loop area than the as-deposited samples during low-field cycles.
The annealed samples will retain a significant magnetocaloric response under low applied fields.
Annealing may cause a modest reduction in the peak entropy-change amplitude.
The as-deposited transition produces a large but narrow entropy-change response.
The as-deposited alloys have limited heat-exchange rates because of a lower surface-to-volume ratio.
The predicted behavior is limited to similarly deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys annealed without grain coarsening or phase decomposition.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as already predominantly ordered, while the intervention is framed as inducing compositional ordering. This is not necessarily impossible, but the hypothesis does not distinguish pre-existing long-range phase order from the proposed nanoscale or grain-boundary compositional order.

The baseline attributes limited heat exchange and low surface-to-volume ratio to the as-deposited alloys, although that limitation is introduced in the task context for bulk ingots and ribbons. The hypothesis does not specify an as-deposited geometry that would justify transferring this baseline property.
